title: Migration pricing pathways: hosted → dedicated onboarding scenarios
author: Marco Lang
body:
Overview
--------
This document describes recommended onboarding pathways, pricing scenarios, and operational checks for customers migrating from Redwood hosted inference to Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. The goal is to give product, sales, and customer-success teams a reproducible decision framework and concrete contract/billing options for common customer archetypes (early-stage scaleups, mid-market SaaS, regulated enterprise).

Goals
- Reduce time-to-production for Dedicated migrations to under 8 weeks for typical customers.
- Align pricing with predictable unit economics while protecting Redwood capacity SLAs.
- Provide clear migration paths that preserve customer latency SLOs and cost transparency.

Scope
- Applies to migrations from Redwood API (hosted) to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools).
- Covers pricing scenarios, onboarding sequencing, required telemetry, contract clauses, and go/no-go criteria.
- Excludes on-prem (Private) deployments; separate reference exists.

Customer archetypes and recommended pathway summary
------------------------------------------------
1) High-throughput transactional SaaS (50M+ tokens/month; strict latency 95th < 200ms):
   - Recommended pathway: Warm-capacity subscription + 12-month reserved commit -> Dedicated baseline with burst lanes
   - Pricing: Fractional slot pricing (base reserve for 80% traffic, burst credits for spikes)
   - Onboarding emphasis: Prefix/KV cache warm-up, synthetic traffic test, integration with customer-side retry/backoff policies.

2) Growth-stage product teams (2M–50M tokens/month; latency tolerant 95th < 400ms):
   - Recommended pathway: Pilot Dedicated (3-month trial) with pro-rated credits, then monthly committed pool
   - Pricing: Pilot discount (25%) and conversion credit toward annual commit
   - Onboarding emphasis: Predictive batching profile tuning and quantization recommendations per workload.

3) Regulated or privacy-sensitive customers (any throughput; data residency/KMS required):
   - Recommended pathway: Dedicated with Private control-plane option and HSM/KMS integration checklist
   - Pricing: Enterprise licensing plus customer-managed infra fee where applicable
   - Onboarding emphasis: Audit log validation, contract SLAs for data handling, compliance runbook signoff.

Pricing scenarios (illustrative only — use legal pricing sheet for final numbers)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Scenario A: Fixed-reserve model
  - Customer commits to N reserved units for 12 months; price = base_rate * N * months
  - Pros: Predictable revenue and capacity planning; Cons: Less flexible during usage dips

- Scenario B: Hybrid reserve + burst credits
  - Customer pays for baseline reserve sized for 70–90% typical usage + pay-as-you-go burst credits at a premium rate
  - Pros: Cost-efficient for spiky workloads; Cons: More complex billing reconciliation

- Scenario C: SLA-backed fractional capacity (SLO entitlements)
  - Customer purchases SLO buckets (latency/availability tiers); capacity mapped dynamically across tenants with crediting engine
  - Pros: Tighter alignment of economics to SLO value; Cons: requires telemetry integration and advanced metering

Billing edge cases and reconciliation notes
-----------------------------------------
- Token accounting: Dedicated usage meters both reserved and burst tokens. Reserved tokens consumed first; burst tokens billed at premium rate and flagged in monthly invoice.
- Overcommit protection: For guarantees, Redwood will provide a 5% overcommit buffer across physical pools by default; any sustained >5% variance triggers capacity review and amendment.
- Prorating: Pilot-to-annual conversions prorate pilot fees into annual commitments as credits; template clause included in appendix.

Onboarding sequence (recommended checklist)
----------------------------------------
1) Sales / Contracting stage (owner: GTM + Legal)
   - Define archetype and pick pricing scenario.
   - Include SLA matrix and breach remediation language.
   - Sign pilot/commit contract and exchange project kickoff docs.
2) Pre-migration assessment (owner: Solutions Engineering)
   - Collect: traffic histogram, token distribution, peak concurrency, sample prompts, max sequence lengths.
   - Run local cost estimator snapshot (CLI):
     redwood cost-estimator --input traffic.csv --model curated/fast-1 --quantization int8 --output report.yaml
3) Pilot / validation (owner: Customer Success + Runtime Eng)
   - Deploy canary to Dedicated pool with mirrored traffic (shadow mode) for 7–14 days.
   - Verify: 95th latency, error rate < 0.5%, token cost matches estimate within 20%.
   - Run synthetic soak: 72h at 1.5x expected peak.
4) Cutover and optimization (owner: Customer Ops + Platform)
   - Gradual DNS/route shift over 48–72h with traffic ramp.
   - Enable KV/prefix cache seeding using historical keys.
   - Apply batching and quantization knobs recommended by Runtime team.
5) Post-cutover review (owner: CS + Product)
   - 30-day health check: cost delta, latency SLO adherence, observed savings.
   - Document permanent config and tag in Redwood Console.

Rollout timeline and owner matrix
----------------------------------
- Week 0: Contract signed (GTM owner)
- Week 1–2: Pre-migration assessment, telemetry integration (Solutions Eng)
- Week 3–6: Pilot and soak tests (Runtime Eng + CS)
- Week 7–8: Production cutover and deprecation of hosted routes (Platform + CS)

SLOs and decision gates
------------------------
- Pre-pilot gate: sample telemetry uploaded, acceptable traffic profile coverage >= 95%.
- Pilot acceptance: 95th latency on Dedicated <= hosted baseline + 25ms OR within contractual SLO tier; error rate improvement or parity.
- Cutover go/no-go: sustained pilot metrics for 72h and resolved P1/P2 issues.

Example migration scenarios (concise)
-------------------------------------
- Example 1: Messaging app (spiky peaks, low average) -> choose hybrid reserve + burst credits; enable burst-lane prewarming.
- Example 2: Document search (steady streaming of long sequences) -> choose fixed-reserve sized for sustained throughput; use quantization playbook to lower cost.

Risk register and mitigations
-----------------------------
- Risk: Unexpected token-cost inflation post-cutover
  Mitigation: Hold 30-day conversion credit; enable conservative default batching until tuned.
- Risk: Latency regression at tail percentiles
  Mitigation: Canary the critical endpoints first, increase warm KV cache size, instrument end-to-end trace.
- Risk: Billing disputes on reserved vs burst split
  Mitigation: Provide transparent monthly breakdown (console + invoice) and standard dispute SLA (15 business days).

Telemetry and instrumentation requirements
------------------------------------------
Minimum telemetry to collect before pilot:
- Token-level usage histogram (per-route, per-model)
- Per-request latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- Concurrency and queueing metrics
- Sample prompt set and avg/95th context length
Tooling: Redwood Console export, cost-estimator snapshot, and pilot CSV to be attached to the engagement ticket.

Contracting clauses to include (templates in legal library)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Pilot conversion credit clause (explicit credit % and expiry)
- Overcommit and amendment clause (thresholds, notice period)
- Data handling & residency addendum for regulated customers

Operational checklist for SRE and Runtime teams
-----------------------------------------------
- Reserve capacity mapping: map CID (customer id) to physical pool and tagging policy.
- Alerting: Create dedicated dashboards for pilot with latency >200ms alerts and early-warning for token spend > 120% of predicted baseline.
- Runbook snippet: rollback to hosted route includes toggling route-policy and revoking Dedicated tokens within 60 minutes.

Appendix: Example pilot contract snippet (illustrative)
-----------------------------------------------------
"PilotTerm": "90 days", "PilotFee": "USD 15,000 (credited on conversion)", "ConversionCredit": "25% of PilotFee applied to first-year commit"

Appendix: Example CLI commands for diagnostics
----------------------------------------------
- Snapshot traffic: redwood snapshot traffic --routes api/v1/generate --duration 3d --out pilot-snapshot.json
- Run cost estimate: redwood cost-estimator --snapshot pilot-snapshot.json --variants fast-1,int8 --out estimate-2027-11-01.yaml
